candidates.why: vars is bound at 12570 to &dwg->header_vars, then 12573 calls dwg_add_handleref -> dwg_new_ref -> dwg_decode_add_object_ref, which reallocs dwg->object_ref (src/decode.c:4632). vars itself is not in that pool, so this is only a weak suspicion; reported because the macro at 12555-12564 dereferences vars repeatedly after the allocation.

CHECK_DICTIONARY_HDR at 12557/12562 stores the ref returned by dwg_find_dictionary into vars->DICTIONARY_##name, and dwg_find_dictionary (src/dwg.c:2092) returns dwg_add_handleref(...) which may allocate a new global ref via dwg_new_ref -> dwg_decode_add_object_ref realloc of dwg->object_ref (src/decode.c:4632). Any previously cached ref pointer held across that realloc would be stale; the macro re-reads vars->DICTIONARY_##name at 12558/12560/12561/12564 after the call, so the ordering is worth checking.

In dwg_find_dictionary, u8 is freed at 2091 and then dwg_add_handleref is called at 2092; u8 is not used after the free, but the free at 2091 sits inside the branch that also returns, and the parallel free at 2095 is on the loop path — worth confirming no path re-enters with the freed u8 (e.g. via nod->texts[j] aliasing).

u8 = nod->texts[j] at 2078 is freed at 2095 (and at 2091) when IS_FROM_TU_DWG; if nod->texts[j] still points at that buffer, the next iteration or a later dwg_find_dictionary call re-reads the freed pointer at 2078. The code does not NULL out nod->texts[j] after the free.
